meta.source: BUILDFlow Content Engine master prompt v1.0
meta.cadence: 2 videos per day: 1 Builder + 1 Consumer, 14 per week

existsInBeta: Customer and project management for contractors
A public contractor profile where customers can find them
inProgressOrPlanned: Paid billing and trial enforcement (billing is a stub today)
productTruth.voiceRule: Anything not in the first list is said as 'We're building...', 'We're testing...' or 'We're working on...'. Never 'BuildFlow lets you...' for it. Never claim users, revenue, testimonials or statistics we do not have.

B.name: Builder
B.line: Contractors who run jobs, workers and customers, mostly through WhatsApp, and want more work.

C.name: Consumer
C.line: Homeowners and project owners who need work done and can't tell who to trust.

videos.hook: If you're struggling to manage multiple construction projects, watch this.
videos.curiosity: Your project info is in five places. There's a better way to structure it.
videos.payoff: Customer, tasks, deadlines, updates and progress should all connect.
videos.connection: That's the problem we're building BUILDFlow to solve.
videos.cta: Follow BUILDFlow as we build it.

beats.vo: If you're struggling to manage multiple construction projects, watch this.

beats.visual: Screen recording: scroll WhatsApp chats, a notes app, a paper calendar.
beats.vo: Your project information might be scattered across five different places.

beats.visual: Freeze on a half-typed reply. One beat of black.
beats.vo: And that's where things start falling through the cracks. There's a better way to structure the project.

videos.hypothesis: A named scenario ('Five projects. Three workers. Twenty WhatsApp messages...') holds the first 3 seconds better than the generic 'if you're struggling' hook.
videos.check: Only show screens that match the current beta.

videos.hook: If you're paying someone to build or renovate your property, don't make this mistake.
videos.curiosity: The mistake happens before any work starts.
videos.payoff: Get the scope and a date for each phase in writing before work begins.
videos.connection: We're building BUILDFlow so the plan and the progress sit in one place you can both see.
videos.cta: Save this before your next project.

beats.visual: POV: standing in a half-built house, bare block walls.
beats.vo: If you're paying someone to build or renovate, don't make this mistake.

beats.visual: Homeowner scrolling WhatsApp, hunting for what was agreed.
beats.vo: A lot of arguments start with 'I thought you said...'

beats.visual: Notes app with an empty line labelled Scope.
beats.vo: The mistake isn't the contractor. It's starting with nothing written down. Here's what to write.

beats.visual: Three quick text cards, each ticking on: What work, What's included, Date per phase.
beats.vo: What exactly is being done. What is and isn't included. And a date for every phase, not just a finish date.

beats.visual: Phone showing the idea of a shared project view. Label it 'in development'.
beats.vo: We're building BUILDFlow so the plan and the progress sit in one place you can both see.

beats.visual: Tap the save icon.
beats.vo: Save this before your next project.

videos.caption: Write it down before the first block is laid. Scope, what's included, and a date for each phase.
videos.hypothesis: A POV shot of an unfinished house stops more homeowners than a talking head.
videos.check: Shared project view is not confirmed. Say 'we're building'.

videos.hook: Want customers to trust your construction company before they meet you?
videos.curiosity: Customers decide before the first call. What are they looking at?
videos.payoff: Show your work while it is happening: progress photos, before and after, a clear profile.
videos.connection: BUILDFlow is in beta with a public contractor profile where customers can find you.

beats.visual: Homeowner on a phone, scrolling past three contractor pages with no photos.
beats.vo: Want customers to trust your company before they meet you?

beats.visual: Split screen: a blank page vs a page full of finished jobs.
beats.vo: Customers decide fast. They look at what you can show them.

beats.visual: Hand holds up one finger.
beats.vo: And the thing that builds the most trust isn't the finished photo. I'll show you.

beats.visual: Before / during / after of a tiling or roofing job, quick cuts.
beats.vo: It's the middle. Photos while the work is happening show you're organised and nothing is hidden.

beats.visual: Screen recording of the BUILDFlow beta public profile.
beats.vo: BUILDFlow is in beta with a public profile built for exactly this, so customers can find you and see your work.

beats.visual: Point at camera.
beats.vo: Send this to a contractor who needs it.

videos.caption: Finished photos are expected. Progress photos build trust. Show the middle of the job.
videos.hypothesis: Delaying the answer ('not the finished photo') raises average watch % over stating the tip up front.
videos.check: Confirm the public profile screens match the live beta.

videos.hook: If you want to know whether a contractor is actually trustworthy, don't just look at their finished photos.
videos.curiosity: What should you ask to see instead?
videos.payoff: Ask for in-progress photos, a past customer to talk to, and watch how clearly they reply.
videos.connection: That's why we're building BUILDFlow around real project history, not just a nice final photo.
videos.cta: What's the biggest problem you've had with a contractor?

beats.visual: A perfect finished kitchen photo. Zoom in slowly.
beats.vo: Want to know if a contractor is trustworthy? Don't just look at the finished photos.

beats.visual: Finger swipes through a contractor's page of only polished photos.
beats.vo: Anyone can post their best angle.

beats.visual: Text card: 3 things to ask for.
beats.vo: Here are three things to ask for instead.

beats.visual: Cards tick in: in-progress photos, a past customer to call, how fast and clearly they reply.
beats.vo: Photos from the middle of a job. A past customer you can actually speak to. And watch how clearly they answer you.
beats.text: Middle photos. Past customer. Clear replies.

beats.visual: Talking head.
beats.vo: We're building BUILDFlow around real project history so you can see more than the last photo.

beats.visual: Question on screen.
beats.vo: What's the biggest problem you've had with a contractor? Tell us below.

videos.caption: A finished photo shows the result. It doesn't show how they got there. Ask for the middle.
videos.hypothesis: A story-prompt CTA pulls more comments than a follow CTA, and those comments become content ideas.
videos.check: 'Project history' is a plan. Keep it as 'we're building'.

videos.hook: Good contractors don't always struggle because they're bad at construction.
videos.curiosity: So why do skilled people still go quiet for weeks?
videos.payoff: Nobody can see their work, so nobody can pick them.
videos.connection: BUILDFlow is in beta with a public profile so customers can find and look at your work.

videos.hook: Your contractor saying 'don't worry, I got it' isn't a project update.
videos.curiosity: So what does a real update sound like?
videos.payoff: A real update says what's done, what's next, what's blocked, and a date.
videos.connection: We're working on BUILDFlow so updates are easy for a contractor to give and easy for you to see.

beats.visual: Phone showing the text: 'Don't worry, I got it 👍'.
beats.vo: 'Don't worry, I got it' isn't a project update.

beats.visual: Homeowner staring at a wall that looks the same as last week.
beats.vo: You still don't know what's done or what's next.

beats.visual: Text card with four empty lines.
beats.vo: A real update has four parts. Most people only get one.

beats.visual: Lines fill: Done. Next. Blocked. Date.
beats.vo: What's done. What's next. What's blocking it. And when the next step happens.

beats.visual: Talking head.
beats.vo: We're working on BUILDFlow so updates are easy for a contractor to give and easy for you to see.

beats.visual: Point at camera.
beats.vo: Send this to someone who's renovating.

videos.caption: Done, next, blocked, date. If you're not getting those four, you don't have an update.
videos.hypothesis: A contrarian hook gets more shares than a how-to hook on the same update topic.
videos.check: Updates for clients are not confirmed in the product. Use 'we're working on'.

videos.hook: Want to know where construction businesses lose money without realizing it?
videos.curiosity: It isn't the big costs. It's four small leaks.
videos.payoff: Rework, workers waiting, late materials and forgotten follow-ups.
videos.connection: We're building BUILDFlow so tasks, deadlines and follow-ups connect to the job.
videos.cta: Save this before your next project.

videos.hook: Your construction project being 'a little delayed' can become VERY expensive.
videos.curiosity: What should you ask the moment someone says 'a little delay'?
videos.payoff: Ask what caused it, what the new date is, and what it changes in the cost.
videos.connection: We're building BUILDFlow so delays and new dates are recorded in the project.

beats.visual: Calendar with the finish date crossed out.
beats.vo: 'A little delayed' can become very expensive.

beats.visual: Homeowner on the phone: 'Just another week.'
beats.vo: It's rarely just one week.

beats.visual: Three question cards stacked up.
beats.vo: The moment you hear 'a little delay', ask three things.

beats.visual: Cards flip: What caused it? What's the new date? Does it change the cost?
beats.vo: What caused it. What's the new date. And does it change the cost. Get the answers in writing.

beats.visual: Talking head.
beats.vo: We're building BUILDFlow so delays and new dates get recorded in the project.

beats.visual: Point at camera.
beats.vo: Send this to someone building right now.

videos.caption: 'A little delay' needs three answers: cause, new date, cost. In writing.
videos.hypothesis: Specific-scenario hooks ('Your contractor says just another week...') beat the warning hook for 3-second retention.
videos.check: Delay tracking is a plan. Keep as 'we're building'.
